blocks.text: Describes all four sub-modules and their roles, gives a typical usage example (load_layers, decide), explains why decide the function is not re-exported, and states the one rule that matters: allow is returned only on an explicit match or a mode default that says allow; everything unknown is ask or deny.

blocks.text: Four import statements collect the public symbols from decide (Context, Decision, Request), modes (MODES, TOOLS, effective_risk, mode_default), rules (the full rule-layer API), and shellparse (ParseResult, Part, parse_shell). There are no other definitions in this file.

gotchas: 'decide' the function is not re-exported from this __init__ — import it as 'from m2c.policy.decide import decide' to avoid shadowing the decide module
The engine never logs, never touches the filesystem, and imports nothing outside the standard library (all four sub-modules are pure)
how_it_works: Imports MODES, TOOLS, effective_risk, mode_default from .modes
Imports the full rule layer API (MergedRules, Rule, RuleLayers, RuleSet, RuleSyntaxError, load_layers, load_rule_file, merge_layers, parse_rule) from .rules
Imports ParseResult, Part, and parse as parse_shell from .shellparse
purpose: Provides a single import point for all policy-engine types so callers never need to reach into decide.py, modes.py, rules.py, or shellparse.py individually. The decide function itself is intentionally not re-exported here to prevent a naming conflict with the decide module.
summary: Public surface of the m2c.policy package: re-exports the decision types, tool catalog, rule loading, shell parser, and mode defaults from the four internal modules.
unknowns: How the managed layer is populated (what 'managed=None' means in practice) is in rules.py, not visible here
